content.title: About
content.content: Barfi (also spelled burfi) is a traditional Indian confection made from milk, sugar, and aromatic additives, often enriched with nuts, dried fruits, or spices. It is traditionally prepared by slowly reducing milk to a thick paste, then incorporating flavorings and shaping the mixture into small squares or rounds.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Barfi is commonly made at home, but it is also sold in Indian sweet shops and market stalls.
There are many flavor variations: classic cardamom, pistachio, coconut, mango, and even chocolate.
The name “burfi” derives from the Persian word “burf,” meaning “sweet.”
In some regions, barfi is served as tiny cubes dusted with powdered sugar.
The dessert is a staple at celebrations such as weddings and religious festivals.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: The milk base provides a notable amount of calcium, essential for bone health.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Milk protein contributes to muscle maintenance.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: Sugar and milk deliver quick energy, useful during periods of high physical activity.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Milk supplies riboflavin (B2) and B12, supporting metabolic processes.

items.title: Antioxidant spices
items.content: Cardamom, saffron, and cloves, often added to barfi, have antioxidant properties.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Barfi is very sweet, so people with diabetes or those watching their weight should limit intake.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: The dairy base can cause discomfort for individuals who are lactose intolerant.

items.title: Nut allergies
items.content: Varieties containing nuts (pistachios, almonds) may trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Barfi is calorie‑dense; portion control is recommended to avoid over‑consumption.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Barfi is served in small bite‑size pieces, often dusted with powdered sugar. It can be enjoyed on its own, added to fruit salads, used as a filling for sweet rolls, or paired with tea.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store barfi in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life keep it refrigerated, where it stays fresh for up to 2 weeks. Discard if it develops a sour smell or visible mold.
